title: A MILLION DOORS, ONE HOSPITAL
final_critic_line: A million incompatible doors and one hospital: Illuminara finds the order hidden in the corridors, then hands the schedule to the people who must live by it.

rounds.summary: A fast, physical, multi-party rescue that differs in texture from S1 (strategic latency) and S2 (legal reasoning): causal scheduling of incompatible physics, with medical teams, refugee delegates and individual patients all keeping agency. The result is clearly positive (every survivable patient treated, no world sacrificed) and the remaining cost (a long resettlement) is honest.

Three concrete hazards are established before the million-door scale expands; the causal coloring emerges through failed models, order-reversal tests, a fortieth-test correction and a live mid-rescue repair rather than assertion. Positive result: Every patient judged survivable at first contact receives treatment, no inhabited door is sacrificed to save another, and the solution becomes a distributed medical capability rather than permanent dependence on Illuminara. Illuminara's contribution: She changes the representation from worlds to order-sensitive boundary transitions, discovers the seventeen-behavior grammar, designs the rotating sanctuary and physically closes the dangerous force paths until local systems can replace her. Other agency: Sira's clinicians set medical priority, Ilex's delegates challenge structural bias, Renn rejects an unconsented use of a patient and later operates the repair, door communities inspect and approve risk, and patients or their representatives retain transfer consent. Remaining consequence: Eighteen arrivals are beyond recovery and seventy-three thousand routes cannot return home; a consent-based resettlement project begins without erasing the success of saving every survivable patient.

A strong first draft with a genuinely good core: the opening line, the three concrete patients whose treatments interfere (Omi, Nhelo, Sirr) before the scale expands, the move from a taxonomy of worlds to the grammar of what happens when one boundary follows another, pairs-versus-loops as the hidden variable, the fortieth-test failure at Door 701 resolved by asking what the bladder means by pressure, Renn's refusal to use one child's treatment to clean the room for another, and the plant-and-payoff of Sirr's four-second delay inside the ring maneuver. The outcome rule (3a) is met in substance: every survivable patient is treated, no inhabited door is sacrificed, and the method passes to local teams, because of Illuminara's representation change and her design. The weakness is that the story is told too fast and too summarized for its length. At 3,174 words it is well over the normal 1,500-2,500 range, yet the central intelligence is announced more than shown: the seventeen verbs are never even partly seen, scene 2 summarizes the failed triage, scene 4 is procedure and statistics, and the finale stacks aphorisms and numbers. The people on the doors are mostly functions.

Positive result: Every survivable patient receives treatment; no inhabited door is sacrificed; local teams can operate and revise the method without Illuminara. Illuminara's contribution: She changes the representation from world taxonomy and pairwise compatibility to ordered boundary-transition paths, discovers relation-bound behavior, designs the repairable sanctuary and physically closes dangerous force paths. Other agency: Sira and clinicians set medical priority; Ilex and door communities challenge estimates; patients and relatives control consent; Renn rejects instrumental use and operates the repaired system; Sirr's team supplies decisive timing; Door 402 controls its shutter. Remaining consequence: Eighteen patients were beyond recovery on arrival, many routes home remain collapsed, and resettlement remains a political and human task.

A clear improvement and a sound base for a final. The revision answers the main T02 objections: the nine-class map now fails on the floor at Nhelo's doorway under Door 701's clock, Door 701 has one minute-based margin that visibly collapses twice, the first ring repair fails and Sirr's team supplies the phase timing, Door 402 wins anchors and joint shutter control before consenting, and the finale is Renn running a transition without Illuminara. Length is back in range. Outcome rule (3a) holds. What remains is concentrated in three places: the pressure-is-a-relation turn is handed to Illuminara by the translator, two causal hinges are unmotivated (why the thread test moves Door 701's clock; why Door 88,201 loses its anchor), and scene 6 still ends on tallies and aphorisms.

Other agency: Sira and clinicians set medical priority; Ilex and door communities challenge estimates; patients and relatives control consent; Renn rejects instrumental use and operates the repaired system; Sirr's team supplies decisive timing; Door 402 controls its shutter. A million incompatible doors and one hospital: Illuminara finds the order hidden in the corridors, then hands the schedule to the people who must live by it. The final answers all three priority points of T04: the relation-bound pressure insight is now derived from the contrast between successful and failed traces before the home translator confirms it; the copper thread visibly crosses Door 701's service lip and Door 88,201's anchor failure follows from the flagged shared anchor chain; scene 6 is trimmed to a witnessed crossing (Erel) and the closing aphorism is gone. Outcome rule 3a holds: every survivable patient is treated, no inhabited door is sacrificed, local teams run and revise the method without her; costs remain (eighteen beyond recovery, collapsed routes, resettlement). Other parties keep real agency (Sira, Ilex, Renn, Door 402, Sirr's team, patients' relatives). Remaining minor weakness, not a blocker: the last two paragraphs repeat the 'no alarm answered elsewhere' beat. Aesthetic only; no prose change requested after the close.
